scenes.text: It is 1834, and you are born in New Bedford, Massachusetts. Your name is Hetty Howland Robinson.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: whaling town house parlor, 1830s, harbor view through window

scenes.text: You will die as the richest woman in America, worth over one hundred million dollars, wearing a dress held together by safety pins.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: whaling town house parlor, 1830s, harbor view through window

scenes.text: Forty years from now, in 1874, you are standing in a New York courtroom facing execution of your assets while armed men watch.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: dark 1870s New York courtroom with wood paneling and gavel

scenes.text: Your lawyers whisper that you might lose every single penny you inherited.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: dark 1870s New York courtroom with wood paneling and gavel

scenes.text: That panic is forty years away. Keep count of three things: your father's ledger, a forged will, and your husband's debt.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: abstract dark space with floating financial counters and years

scenes.text: At age six, your eyesight is fine, but your father's is terrible. He makes you read financial newspapers and stock listings to him every evening.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Quaker parlor with oil lamps and stacks of financial papers

scenes.text: By age thirteen, you are your family's official bookkeeper. You memo every penny. Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Quaker parlor with oil lamps and stacks of financial papers

scenes.text: Let us explain compound interest: money making children, and those children making more children.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank interior with a vault and growing stacks of coins

scenes.text: If you lock one dollar in a box at six percent annual interest: interest paid once a year, it becomes two dollars in twelve years without you doing any work.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank interior with a vault and growing stacks of coins

scenes.text: You realize early that spending cash stops compound interest cold. So you stop spending.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank interior with a vault and growing stacks of coins

scenes.text: When your father gives you twelve hundred dollars for fine clothes, you buy government bonds instead and wear old rags, which is a great way to impress party guests.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: fancy Victorian ball room with elegant guests looking shocked

scenes.text: In 1865, your father dies, leaving you five million dollars: about one hundred million today.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: somber Victorian home during a period of mourning

scenes.text: Your Aunt Sylphatina dies shortly after, leaving two million dollars to charity instead of you. You are furious.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: somber Victorian home during a period of mourning

scenes.text: You produce an earlier codicil: an addition to a will, granting you everything, and sign your aunt's name.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: dim lawyer office with legal papers and ink bottle

paper.text: I LEAVE MY ENTIRE ESTATE TO CHARITY

scenes.text: The family sues you for forgery. Remember that forged will.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: dim lawyer office with legal papers and ink bottle

scenes.text: In 1867, you marry Edward Henry Green, a wealthy silk trader, after making him sign a contract promising he will never claim a dime of your money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: wedding parlor decorated with modest flowers

scenes.text: To escape the forgery lawsuit, you flee to London. The panic that threatens your estate is seven years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: foggy London street with horse-drawn carriages

scenes.text: In London, while America recovers from the Civil War, you buy greenbacks: paper dollars issued during wartime that everyone thinks are worthless.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: London financial exchange floor with traders trading US debt

scenes.text: You buy them for fifty cents on the dollar. When the government honors them at full value, you make millions.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: London financial exchange floor with traders trading US debt

scenes.text: Internet myth number one says you were so cheap that when your son Ned injured his knee, you refused to pay a doctor and caused his leg to be amputated.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: plain living room in London flat

scenes.text: It didn't happen. You took him to free clinics disguised in old clothes, but when doctors recognized you, you hired top specialists for years before amputation became unavoidable.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: plain living room in London flat

paper.text: MYTH: REFUSED ALL DOCTORS FOR NED

scenes.text: In 1874, you return to New York. The court rules the forged codicil invalid, but you settle without losing your main fortune.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New York court house room after trial settlement

scenes.text: Remember your father's ledger, your aunt's forged will, and your husband's debt? Now the debt comes due.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: John J. Cisco & Son bank building entrance

scenes.text: Your husband Edward secretly uses your deposits as collateral: assets pledged to secure a loan, for his bad investments.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: John J. Cisco & Son bank building entrance

scenes.text: When his bank fails, they seize your money to pay his two million dollar debt. Your prenuptial agreement pays off.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: teller window inside financial firm

scenes.text: You pay his debt to save your credit, but you instantly throw Edward out of your house and live separately forever.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: doorway of Brooklyn boarding house

quote.text: MY HUSBAND IS THE POOREST BUSINESS MAN IN NEW YORK

scenes.text: Internet myth number two claims you never washed your hands and only ate cold oatmeal heated on a radiator.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cheap Manhattan pie shop counter

scenes.text: It didn't happen. You ate cheap fifteen-cent pies at local bakeries, but you washed thoroughly and wore black mourning clothes simply to avoid buying fashion updates.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cheap Manhattan pie shop counter

paper.text: MYTH: LIVED IN DIRT AND ONLY ATE COLD OATMEAL

scenes.text: Press reporters call you The Witch of Wall Street because of your grim black cloak.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: crowded Wall Street sidewalk with newspaper boys

scenes.text: During the Panic of 1893, when major banks collapse, you have millions in cash ready while everyone else is desperate.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Chemical Bank of New York vault room filled with cash drawers

scenes.text: The City of New York comes begging to you for a loan. You lend them one million dollars at strict terms.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Chemical Bank executive desk with city officials

quote.text: I BUY WHEN THINGS ARE LOW AND NOBODY WANTS THEM

scenes.text: During the Panic of 1907, desperate bankers queue outside your bank floor to borrow your reserves.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: crowded bank corridor with panicked Wall Street figures

scenes.text: You write a single check to save New York City from bankruptcy again. You are the lender of last resort.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: crowded bank corridor with panicked Wall Street figures

scenes.text: In 1916, at age eighty-one, you die following an argument with a maid over skimmed milk.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: modest apartment parlor in New York

scenes.text: Your liquid fortune of over one hundred million dollars: about two point five billion today, makes you the wealthiest woman in world history.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bank vault full of government bonds and cash stacks

scenes.text: So how did a girl from New Bedford win Wall Street? By compounding cash while others chased luxury.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: modern Wall Street skyline with stock ticker

scenes.text: Today, her value investing strategy is still used by Warren Buffett and modern hedge funds.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: modern Wall Street skyline with stock ticker

scenes.text: Never buy what you cannot hold, and never let money sit idle.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: black title screen background
scenes.title: YOUR LIFE AS HETTY GREEN
